text:
The Flyers arrive in Calgary with one story drowning out everything else, and it belongs to a 21-year-old. Matvei Michkov has 11 points (8 goals) in his last ten games, he's their leading goal scorer, and the weekend headlines are about his ice time under Rick Tocchet: Broad Street Hockey wrote that he "sends clear message to Flyers about limited ice time." PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor put it plainly: if there's tension in the room, "The group has to figure this out." Our numbers say the hot streak is earned. He's getting 3.6 expected goals on his own shots over those ten games against a usual 2.8. The question in Calgary is simply how much he plays.

The Flyers need him to. They're 1-3-1 in their last five, game two of a five-game road trip, and our playoff odds give them about 2%. They're better than the record (43% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, with finishing 8.5 goals behind their chances), but that's cold comfort in November. Trevor Zegras, who The New York Times reported sat for 10 minutes after "showing the ref up" last week, has the best goal chance on the team at 27%.

Calgary has its own bad news. Kevin Bahl will miss the rest of the season with a ruptured Achilles, per Daily Faceoff, and the Flames blew a two-goal lead in a 5-3 loss to Anaheim on Friday. Devin Cooley, back from injured reserve, starts in net (+2.2 goals saved above expected, which measures saves beyond what the shots deserved) against Dan Vladar (-0.2). Two former Flyers lead Calgary's chances: Joel Farabee (30% to score, best on either side) and Morgan Frost.

Our numbers have it close, 2.91 to 2.76 expected goals for Calgary. Both teams take more than four penalties a game, and Calgary's power play produces only 0.39 expected goals a night, so the special teams may decide less than you'd think.
headline: Michkov's minutes are the story in Calgary

hunch.text: Michkov answers the ice-time questions the only way that settles them: he scores in Calgary, whatever his minutes look like.
